leads.title: A cast or rounding point moved
leads.reason: The same call produces ['torch.bfloat16'] on the reference and ['torch.float32'] on the suspect. The two runs round at different places, and one side has call sites the other never runs.
leads.check: Write down both sequences (where each cast happens, what is fused, the accumulator dtype) and compare the next boundary with equal dtype element by element (bi_check.first_mismatch).
fix_options: Make the suspect round where the reference rounds.
If the new order is wanted, change both runs together and accept a new reference.

leads.title: Uncontrolled surface: torch.deterministic_algorithms.warn_only
leads.reason: Ops without a deterministic implementation only warn and stay nondeterministic. Measured: the backward of SDPA flash and memory-efficient attention differs run to run in dQ (handbook/cases/attention-backward.md).

leads.title: A backward kernel upstream
leads.reason: The operator reads gradients (norms[name] = torch.linalg.vector_norm(param.grad)), and its input differs while the forward events before it agree: a backward kernel upstream produced different bits from the same forward. At this call site 135 of 144 calls differ and 9 agree; the calls that agree mark values that do not depend on the nondeterministic op.
leads.check: Map each call at this site to its parameter (call order) and find the most downstream parameter that differs. Then repeat that op's backward 5 times on fixed inputs (bi_check.check_repeat).
fix_options: torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False): warn_only=True leaves SDPA's backward nondeterministic (measured).
For index_add / scatter_add / embedding-style backward: the deterministic flag, or a sorted fixed-order accumulation.
